subject: Review: public console language on subprocessors & data transfers
content:
From: Natalie Barker <natalie.barker@acme.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: acme-legal@acme.com, procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API copy question: subprocessors + cross-border blurb

Hi Ava,

We kicked off a procurement review and a couple of questions came up from legal about the public-facing console copy that lists subprocessors and describes cross-border transfers. Procurement wants a short, plain-language blurb we can include in our vendor questionnaire and in the SOW, and legal would like the console wording not to sound like it creates new contractual terms (they're worried about phrases like "we may transfer" vs "we transfer").

Can you share a short version — ideally one sentence + one short FAQ — and the current subprocessor map? Our deadline is next Thursday.

Thanks,
Natalie Barker
Sr. Vendor Ops, Acme Corporation

[Attachment: procurement-qa-template.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Natalie Barker <natalie.barker@acme.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API copy question: subprocessors + cross-border blurb

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Laura (product marketing).

Quick plan:
- Kimberly: can you review the one-sentence blurb below and confirm it's not "contract-y"?
- Laura: can you convert any approved text into a one-slide sales-friendly snippet for procurement?
- Rishi: do we have a recent subprocessor export (CSV) and a short FAQ we can share?

Draft one-sentence blurb (plain language):
"Redwood Inference operates a limited set of subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers and managed service vendors) to deliver the Hosted API; we list current subprocessors and the regions where they process data in the subprocessor map."

Short FAQ suggestion (2 bullets):
• Where can I see who processes our data? — See the subprocessor map (attached).
• Will Redwood transfer data outside my region? — We may route processing to other regions to deliver the service; you can request a residency restriction under our Dedicated/Private options.

Attaching our latest subprocessor map (export) and a working public-terms draft.

Best,
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: subprocessor-map-2026.csv (csv), public-terms-draft-v3.docx (docx)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, Natalie Barker <natalie.barker@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API copy question: subprocessors + cross-border blurb

Thanks for the draft, Ava. A few legal notes inline:

- "Operate a limited set of subprocessors" — ok, but prefer "uses" instead of "operates" (less operational implication).
- Avoid "we may route" on the public console; that can read as a promise of unpredictability. Suggest: "Processing may occur in multiple regions; details are in the subprocessor map and residency options are available for Dedicated/Private deployments."
- Add a short sentence clarifying that the subprocessor map is updated regularly and that contractual commitments about data location are captured in the DPA/contract.

Revised one-sentence blurb (legal-safe):
"Redwood Inference uses a limited set of subprocessors (for example, cloud providers and managed services) to provide the Hosted API; our current subprocessor map shows where processing occurs and is updated regularly. Contractual commitments about where customer data is maintained are set out in the DPA and customer agreements."

Short FAQ (legal-checked):
• Where can I see who processes my data? — See the subprocessor map.
• Will Redwood transfer data outside my region? — Processing may occur in multiple regions. Customers requiring contractual residency guarantees should contact sales about Dedicated or Private deployment options.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

-----
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Love the legal-safe version — thanks Kim. I'll make two variants: one for the console (short) and one for procurement decks (slightly expanded).

Console micro-copy (single-line):
"We use a limited set of subprocessors; see the subprocessor map for current locations."

Procurement-friendly paragraph (short):
"Redwood uses vetted subprocessors (cloud providers and managed services) to operate the Hosted API. Our subprocessor map lists current providers and the regions where we process data. If your organization requires contractual residency guarantees, we offer Dedicated and Private deployment options — contact sales for details and to review DPA terms."

I'll drop these into the shared Drive and create a one-slide export for Acme procurement.

Laura Bennett
Product Marketing Lead, Redwood Inference

Sharing the CSV export and a small script we use to build the public map. Note: the public map intentionally omits certain infra providers used only for internal metrics (we list customer-facing subprocessors only).

Two quick notes for procurement:
1) The subprocessor map shows processing regions as a best-effort classification; grey areas mean "may be used depending on capacity".
2) If Acme needs full contract-level residency restrictions, we will need to move to Dedicated or Private and scope the DPA — that's handled via sales/Solutions.
